hints: Apply conservation of linear momentum to the collision between P and Q, taking the initial direction of P as positive.
Note that after the collision, P can either continue moving in the original direction with velocity $+1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ or rebound with velocity $-1\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute both possible values of $v_P$ into $0.2(6) = 0.2 v_P + 0.5 v_Q$ to find the two possible speeds of Q.
walkthrough:
Apply conservation of linear momentum with initial total momentum $0.2 \times 6 + 0.5 \times 0 = 1.2\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$:
$$0.2 \times 6 = 0.2 v_P + 0.5 v_Q \implies 1.2 = 0.2 v_P + 0.5 v_Q$$

Case 1: Particle P continues in the same direction with $v_P = +1\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$1.2 = 0.2(1) + 0.5 v_Q \implies 0.5 v_Q = 1.0 \implies v_Q = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Case 2: Particle P rebounds in the reverse direction with $v_P = -1\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$1.2 = 0.2(-1) + 0.5 v_Q \implies 0.5 v_Q = 1.4 \implies v_Q = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the principle of conservation of linear momentum: in the absence of external horizontal forces, the total momentum before collision equals the total momentum after collision:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$

Substitute the given masses $m_P = 0.2\text{ kg}$ and $m_Q = 0.5\text{ kg}$, with initial velocities $u_P = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_Q = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$0.2(6) + 0.5(0) = 1.2\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$$

Because the question specifies that the speed of P is $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ without stating its direction, there are two distinct physical possibilities for its velocity after impact: forward ($v_P = +1\text{ m s}^{-1}$) or backward ($v_P = -1\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

Case 1 (P continues forward, $v_P = +1\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$1.2 = 0.2(1) + 0.5 v_Q$$
$$1.2 = 0.2 + 0.5 v_Q$$
Subtract $0.2$ from both sides:
$$0.5 v_Q = 1.0$$
Divide by $0.5$:
$$v_Q = \frac{1.0}{0.5} = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Both speeds are positive and physically possible: $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.Conserving Linear Momentum: Sets up $0.2(6) = 0.2(\pm 1) + 0.5v_Q$ and evaluates the two speeds as $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
